ABD merkezli teknoloji devi Microsoft'un Outlook, Teams ve Copilot gibi hizmetlerinde yaklaşık 20 saattir erişim sorunu yaşanıyor.
Microsoft, yaptığı son güncellemede etkilenen sunucularda bazı değişiklikler gerçekleştirdiğini ancak bunların kalıcı düzelme sağlamadığını duyurdu. Şirket, söz konusu değişikliklerin yapıldığı bölgelerde kısmi bir iyileşme gözlemlendiğini belirtti.
Microsoft, X üzerinden yaptığı açıklamada, "Genel altyapı istikrarını artırmak için başka hangi ek adımları atabileceğimizi değerlendiriyoruz" ifadesini kullandı.
Şirketten ilerleyen saatlerde yapılan bir başka açıklamada, sorunun henüz çözülemediği, birden fazla hizmete erişimde aksaklık yaşandığı ve tam kapasite hizmet verilemediği kaydedildi.
Microsoft, kesintinin siber saldırı kaynaklı olduğuna dair herhangi bir kanıt bulunmadığını da bildirdi.
Avustralya İçişleri Bakanı Tony Burke de benzer bir açıklama yaptı.
Konuyu Microsoft yetkilileri ile görüştüğünü belirten Burke, "Bir siber saldırıyla karşı karşıya olduklarını düşünmüyorlar. Bunun, bir güncellemenin yanlış gitmesi nedeniyle 2024'teki CrowdStrike olayına benzer bir durum olduğunu düşünüyorlar" dedi.
Temmuz 2024'te yaşanan büyük çaplı kesinti dünya çapında havalimanlarında uçuşların durmasına, hastanelerde ve bankalarda aksamalara yol açmıştı. Teksas merkezli siber güvenlik şirketi CrowdStrike, sorunun Microsoft Windows işletim sistemi kullanan bilgisayarları etkileyen hatalı bir güncellemeden kaynaklandığını açıklamıştı.
Microsoft hizmetlerindeki sorun; ABD, Japonya ve Avustralya'daki devlet kurumlarının yanı sıra OpenAI ve Anthropic gibi yapay zeka şirketlerini de etkiliyor. İngiltere'de de sağlık hizmetlerinde kesinti kaynaklı ciddi aksaklıklar yaşandığı bildirildi.
Bu, "Microsoft 365" hizmetlerinde bu yıl yaşanan ikinci aksaklık oldu. Bu durum, Microsoft'un güvenilirliğinin özellikle de kurumsal müşterilerce sorgulanması riskine yol açıyor.
Şirketin internet sayfasında yer alan bilgiye göre, Outlook ve Teams gibi popüler uygulamaları içeren bulut tabanlı abonelik hizmeti Microsoft 365'i dünya çapında 430 milyondan fazla kişi kullanıyor.
Kesinti takip platformu Downdetector'a göre, Microsoft ürünleri 74 ülke ve bölgede devre dışı kaldı. Downdetector, kesintiden Kuzey Amerika ile Güney Amerika'nın yanı sıra Avrupa, Asya ve Afrika'nın da etkilendiğini bildirdi.

Gürlek, NSosyal hesabından, "Hiçbir cinayetin üzerinin zamanla örtülmesine izin vermeyeceğiz. 76 dosyada 83 cinayeti faili meçhul olmaktan çıkardık" başlığıyla paylaşımda bulundu.
Yıllar önce işlenen cinayetlerin aydınlatılması, geride kalan ailelerin cevapsız sorularına yanıt bulunması ve sorumluların adalet önünde hesap vermesi için yürüttükleri çalışmaları kararlılıkla sürdürdüklerini vurgulayan Gürlek, şunları kaydetti:
"Bu amaçla, Bakanlığımız bünyesindeki Faili Meçhul Suçları Araştırma Daire Başkanlığımızın koordinasyonunda, Cumhuriyet başsavcılıklarımız ve kolluk birimlerimizin işbirliğiyle Bursa ve Bitlis'te 14, 16 ve 20 yıldır aydınlatılamayan 3 ayrı cinayet dosyasını yeniden ele aldık. Gelişen teknolojik imkanlardan yararlanarak DNA analizlerini, kriminal inceleme raporlarını, HTS ve baz istasyonu kayıtları ile tanık beyanlarını birlikte değerlendirdik. Elde edilen deliller doğrultusunda şüphelilere yönelik operasyonlar düzenledik."
Bursa'nın Mustafakemalpaşa ilçesinde 2010'da ormanlık alanda av tüfeğiyle öldürülmüş halde bulunan Mehmet Arıcan'ın dosyasında HTS kayıtları, mali incelemeler ve yeni tanık beyanlarının yeniden değerlendirildiğini bildiren Gürlek, gerçekleştirilen operasyonda gözaltına alınan şüphelilerden birinin tutuklandığını belirtti.
Gürlek, Bitlis'in Tatvan ilçesinde 2006'da başından ateşli silahla vurulmuş halde yol kenarında bulunan kadının dosyasında DNA örnekleri, HTS kayıtları ve tanık beyanlarının yeniden incelendiğini ifade etti.
Eş zamanlı düzenlenen operasyonlarda gözaltına alınan şüphelilerden 2'sinin tutuklandığını, 2'si hakkında adli kontrol kararı verildiğini kaydeden Gürlek, yurt dışında bulunan firari şüpheli hakkında yakalama ve kırmızı bülten çıkarılmasına yönelik çalışmaların sürdüğünü aktardı.
Bakan Gürlek, maktulün kimliğinin belirlenmesi için incelemelerin devam ettiğini bildirdi.
Bursa'nın Kestel ilçesinde 2012'de kaybolan Mehmet Şahinoğlu'nun öldürülmesine ilişkin soruşturmada, 2015'te Kestel'de bulunan yanmış insan kemiklerine yönelik adli tıp incelemeleri, diş kayıtları, iletişim verileri ve tanık beyanlarının yeniden ele alındığının bilgisini paylaşan Gürlek, "Elde edilen bulgular doğrultusunda 12 şüpheliye yönelik operasyon düzenlendi. 11 şüpheli gözaltına alındı, firari bir şüphelinin yakalanmasına yönelik çalışmalar sürüyor." ifadelerini kullandı.
Soruşturmaları titizlikle yürüten kamu görevlilerine teşekkür eden Gürlek, "Zamanın geçmesi, suçların cezasız kalmasına gerekçe olamaz. Geçmişte işlenen cinayetlerin aydınlatılması için yürütülen çalışmaların takipçisi olmaya, adaletin tecellisi için üzerimize düşen sorumlulukları yerine getirmeye devam edeceğiz." değerlendirmesini yaptı.

Kitap dünyasına açılan kapınızı aralayın! En sevdiğiniz kitapları indirimli fiyatlarla keşfedin ve hayal gücünüzü genişletin.
İstanbul Büyükşehir Belediye (İBB) Başkanı ve cumhurbaşkanı adayı Ekrem İmamoğlu, ilk celsede yapamadığı savunmasının yer aldığı “Millet Şahidimdir” kitabına ilişkin soruşturma kapsamında verdiği ifadenin ardından, İBB Davası’ndaki sözleri nedeniyle başlatılan ikinci soruşturmada da ifade verdi.
Silivri Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı Memur Suçları Soruşturma Bürosu tarafından yürütülen soruşturma kapsamında İmamoğlu'nun ifadesi, avukatı Tora Pekin eşliğinde Silivri Adliyesi SEGBİS odasında alındı.
Hakkında açılan soruşturmaların sayısının 20’ye ulaştığını belirten İmamoğlu, “Ağırlıklı olarak da çeşitli ifadelerim soruşturma konusu yapılıyor. Hiçbir şiddet övgüsü hiçbir şiddet çağrısı içermeyen siyasi nitelikteki açıklamalarım, eleştirilerim, soruşturma ve dava konusu yapılıyor” dedi.
Savcılıkların sözlerinden suç çıkarmaya çalıştığını savunan İmamoğlu, “Gittikçe daha fazla zorluyorlar. Olmadık gerekçelerle işlem yapıyor, sözlerimden sürekli suç çıkarmaya çalışıyorlar” ifadelerini kullandı.
İBB Davası’nda kullandığı sözlerin tehdit olarak değerlendirilmesine tepki gösteren İmamoğlu, şöyle konuştu:
“‘Ben savunma yapmam, ben yargılayacağım, yargılayacağım merak etmeyin, ben iddianame yapanları yargılayacağım’ sözlerim tehdit suçuymuş. Ben yargıç değilim. Mahkeme değilim. Belli ki bir mahkeme kurup yargılama yapacak konumda da değilim. Bu yönüyle çok açık ki ‘yargılama’ kavramını mecazi anlamda kullanıyorum.”
İddianameyi hazırlayanları eleştirdiğini belirten İmamoğlu, “Bana göre içine boca edilmiş iftiralarını, yalanlarını, yanlışlarını yüzlerine vururum. Kendi olgularımı ortaya koyarım” dedi.
İmamoğlu, sözlerinin tehdit olarak değerlendirilmesine ilişkin, “Asıl olan milletin muhakemesi yani verdiği hükümdür. Bu tehdit midir? Savcılar, yargıçlar bunu tehdit olarak kabul ediyorsa bu benim değil onların sorunu” ifadelerini kullandı.
“Kendine güvenen bir savcı, bir yargıç yargılama sözcüğünden korkmaz diye düşünüyorum” diyen İmamoğlu, soruşturmayla tehdit anlamı taşımayan bir kavrama suç yüklenmeye çalışıldığını savundu.
Savcılık, İmamoğlu’na “Ben savunma yapmam, ben yargılayacağım, yargılayacağım merak etmeyin, ben iddianameyi yapanları yargılayacağım” sözleriyle ne demek istediğini ve kimleri kastettiğini sordu.
İmamoğlu, “Ben bu sözlerle o zamanki İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcısı, şu an Adalet Bakanı olan kişinin soruşturmayı yürütme sürecini ve uygulamalarını kastettim. İddianameyi yazanlar ya da mahkeme heyeti yönünde kişisel bir kastım yoktur. Kaldı ki iddianameyi yapanlar tarifinden görev tanımı olarak mahkeme heyetinin anlaşılması da mümkün değildir.” dedi.

Manchester United'ın kaptanı Bruno Fernandes'in geleceği belirsizliğini koruyor. The Athletic'te yer alan habere göre Portekizli yıldız, İngiliz ekibinin kendisine sunduğu ikinci sözleşme uzatma teklifini de geri çevirdi.
Manchester United'ın kaptanı Bruno Fernandes ile yeni sözleşme görüşmeleri, yaz aylarında ilk teklifin yapılması ve Portekizli futbolcu tarafından reddedilmesinden bu yana devam ediyor.
Manchester United, daha yakın zamanda iyileştirilmiş şartlarla yeni bir teklif sundu ancak Fernandes henüz bu tekliften memnun değil. Bu nedenle taraflar arasında yeni görüşmeler yapılması bekleniyor.
32 yaşındaki futbolcunun maaşı ve sözleşme süresi, görüşmelerde ele alınan konular arasında yer alıyor. Fernandes'in mevcut sözleşmesi Haziran 2027'de sona eriyor. Mevcut şartlarda Portekizli oyuncu, ocak ayından itibaren bonservis bedeli ödemeden transfer olma ihtimali için yabancı kulüplerle görüşme hakkına sahip olacak.
Manchester United'ın sözleşmeyi 12 ay daha uzatma opsiyonu bulunuyor. Kulübün bu opsiyonu kullanması durumunda Fernandes'in ocak ayından itibaren yabancı kulüplerle görüşme özgürlüğü ortadan kalkacak. Her durumda Manchester United, Fernandes'in takımda kalmasını istiyor.
Portekizli futbolcu da geleceğiyle ilgili değerlendirmelerini sürdürüyor ve geçmişte takımdan ayrılma ihtimaline açık kapı bırakmıştı. Son sözleşmesini 2024 yılında imzalamıştı.
Fernandes'in bu yaz yalnızca yabancı kulüplerin kullanabileceği 65 milyon euroluk bir serbest kalma maddesi bulunuyordu ancak bu madde daha sonra sona erdi. Manchester United, bu sürenin ardından Fernandes'i satmaya sıcak bakmadı.
Fernandes'in ikinci teklifi de reddetmesi, Manchester United'da dikkat çekici bir tablo ortaya çıkarıyor. Kulüp yönetimi oyuncunun takımda kalmasını istiyor, Fernandes de kariyerine burada devam etmek istiyor. Ancak iki tarafın da bu konuda ne ölçüde istekli olduğu soru işareti oluşturuyor.
Fernandes, bir sonraki sözleşmesinin kariyerindeki son büyük anlaşma olabileceği bir yaşta. Manchester United ise Sir Jim Ratcliffe yönetiminin maaş bütçesini azaltmaya yönelik adımlar attığı bir dönemde, maliyetleri beklenen performansla dengelemek zorunda.
Liverpool'un 2025'in başlarında Mohamed Salah'ın sözleşmesiyle ilgili yürüttüğü süreç, bu duruma benzer bir örnek olarak gösteriliyor.

Manchester United'da Alex Ferguson'un 2013 yılında görevinden ayrılmasının ardından yaşanan teknik direktör değişikliklerinin mali bilançosu dikkat çekici boyutlara ulaştı.
İngiliz kulübü, son olarak Michael Carrick ile yollarını ayırırken Ferguson sonrası dönemde sekizinci teknik direktör ayrılığı gerçekleşti. Kırmızı Şeytanlar'ın bu süreçte teknik direktörler için ödediği bonservis ve tazminatların toplamı 120 milyon Euro'yu aştı.
Böylece kulübün teknik direktör değişikliklerine yaptığı harcama, tarihinin en pahalı transferi olan Paul Pogba için ödediği 105 milyon Euro'luk bonservis bedelini geride bıraktı.
The Telegraph'ın haberine göre, Manchester United, 2013 yılından bu yana teknik direktörlerin göreve getirilmesi ve sözleşmelerinin feshedilmesi için 120 milyon Euro'nun üzerinde ödeme yaptı.
Son olarak 2028 yılına kadar sözleşmesi bulunan Michael Carrick'in görevine son verilmesiyle bu tutara en az 6 milyon Euro daha eklendi.
İngiliz ekibinin yeni teknik direktör adayları arasında öne çıkan Mauricio Pochettino için de yaklaşık 9 milyon Euro bonservis ödemesi gerekebileceği belirtildi. ABD Millî Takımı'nı çalıştıran Arjantinli teknik adamın mevcut sözleşmesi 2030 yılına kadar devam ediyor.
Manchester United'ın teknik direktör değişikliklerinde en yüksek tazminat ödemesi José Mourinho için yapıldı.
Temmuz 2016'da göreve başlayan Portekizli çalıştırıcı, kulüpteki ilk sezonunda UEFA Avrupa Ligi şampiyonluğu yaşarken Premier League'de altıncı ve ikinci sırada tamamlanan sezonların ardından Aralık 2018'de görevinden ayrıldı. İngiliz kulübü, Mourinho'ya sözleşmesinin feshi nedeniyle 23,4 milyon Euro tazminat ödedi.
Mourinho'nun ardından göreve gelen Ole Gunnar Solskjaer için de 10,9 milyon Euro ödeme yapıldı. Norveçli teknik adamın Kasım 2021'de ayrılmasının ardından geçici olarak takımın başına getirilen Ralf Rangnick'in ayrılığı ve sözleşmesine ilişkin düzenlemelerin toplam maliyetinin ise 17,6 milyon Euro'ya kadar ulaştığı aktarıldı.
2022 yazında göreve başlayan Erik ten Hag da Manchester United'ın yüksek maliyetli teknik direktör değişikliklerinden biri oldu. Hollandalı çalıştırıcı, 2024 yılında Manchester City'ye karşı kazanılan FA Cup finalinin ardından sözleşmesini uzatmasına rağmen aynı yılın ekim ayında görevden alındı. Kulübün Ten Hag'a ödediği tazminat 12,4 milyon Euro olarak kayıtlara geçti.
Kasım 2024'te Sporting CP'den transfer edilen Ruben Amorim için Portekiz kulübüne bonuslar hariç 11 milyon Euro bonservis ödendi. Manchester United'ın başında 63 karşılaşmaya çıkan Amorim, Ocak 2026'da görevinden ayrılırken 9,8 milyon Euro tazminat aldı. Böylece Portekizli teknik adamın toplam maliyeti 20,8 milyon Euro'ya ulaştı.
Ferguson'un doğrudan halefi David Moyes için 5,9 milyon Euro, Louis van Gaal için ise 10 milyon Euro tazminat ödendi. Teknik direktörlerin yanı sıra yönetim kadrosundaki değişiklikler de kulübün maliyetlerini artırdı.
Newcastle United'dan 3,6 milyon Euro karşılığında göreve getirilen sportif direktör Dan Ashworth, yalnızca beş ay sonra ayrılırken 4,9 milyon Euro tazminat aldı.
Manchester United'ın yüksek maliyetleri yalnızca teknik direktör değişiklikleriyle sınırlı kalmadı. İngiliz kulübü, Ferguson'un ayrılışından bu yana yeni futbolcular için toplam 2,49 milyar Euro bonservis harcaması yaptı.
Bu dönemde Avrupa'da yalnızca Chelsea ve Manchester City daha fazla transfer harcaması gerçekleştirdi. Buna karşın Manchester United, söz konusu süreçte bir UEFA Avrupa Ligi, ikişer FA Cup, İngiltere Lig Kupası ve Community Shield şampiyonluğu elde edebildi. Kulüp, özellikle Premier League'de beklediği istikrarı sağlayamadı.
Son yedi sezonda 500 milyon Euro'nun üzerinde zarar açıklayan Manchester United, bir yandan da giderlerini azaltmaya yönelik adımlar atıyor. 2025 yılından bu yana 322 çalışanın işine son verilirken personel için sunulan ücretsiz öğle yemeği uygulaması da kaldırıldı. Bu kararla yıllık 1,2 milyon Euro'nun üzerinde tasarruf hedeflendi.
Teknik direktör değişiklikleri ve yüksek transfer harcamalarına rağmen sportif başarıda istikrar yakalayamayan Manchester United, mevcut sezonda Premier League'de düşme hattında bulunuyor. İngiliz kulübü, Pochettino'nun olası göreve gelişiyle yeni bir başlangıç yapmayı hedeflerken teknik direktör değişikliklerinin toplam maliyetinin daha da artması bekleniyor.

Microsoft is slowly recovering from its day-long outage after much of the company’s systems were hit by a cascading software issue.
The problems, which started Thursday, were initially flagged as affecting the company’s services in the U.S. and the Americas, but quickly spread around the world, as engineers struggled to recover downed servers.
What began as an Outlook email and Teams video conferencing outage soon developed into a full blown meltdown, affecting the company’s cloud services for both consumer and business email, files, and documents. The outage also knocked out the company’s Copilot AI tools, Defender security screening software, and prevented system administrators from accessing their internal Intune dashboards and features. Some users reportedly experienced issues with accessing their cloud-based Windows computers.
Microsoft hasn’t yet said what caused the issues, only saying the outage involved “a large number of servers being unexpectedly unavailable.” The company said it continues to investigate the cause.
The outage affected a broad range of industries, including TechCrunch’s own email. We’ve reached out to Microsoft for comment about the incident.
As of Friday morning on the U.S. east coast, Microsoft’s Outlook email service had begun to recover and some emails have been trickling in. The recovery comes after engineers initially could not find the cause of the issue that was causing servers in Microsoft’s data centers to fail.
Doug Madory, the director of internet analysis at Kentik, a company that monitors internet traffic worldwide, said in a post on Bluesky that traffic was returning to Microsoft’s services after about 18 hours of downtime.
Microsoft said in its latest status update on Friday that there was “no evidence of malicious activity associated with this incident.” That may be some solace for the millions who went without their email and online services yesterday, but the company is likely to face questions about its inability to swiftly recover from an outage of its own making.
A Microsoft spokesperson did not respond to our questions asking if the company has the technical means to detect malicious activity, such as logs, or if Microsoft has a way to check what happened.
The last major incident affecting Microsoft services was in September , when a days-long outage hit Microsoft’s cloud services. During that outage, Microsoft blamed a “core authentication configuration” issue that prevented users from accessing the service.
This story was first published on November 12 and has been updated throughout.

The Times of London reports that he allegedly had a third affair and that the fallout may impact US President Donald Trump . Democrats are now planning a congressional investigation into how much Trump knew about the affairs. Huang's downfall is also a blow to his own reputation. The Times says: "He defied Silicon Valley tech mogul stereotypes as an apparently devoted father and husband married for 40 years. Now, his followers are struggling to come to terms with revelations that have tarnished the image of the man they revered."
Elsewhere, Italian daily Il Manifesto says it is "Game Over" for Huang. Both French paper Le Figaro and the British daily Financial Times focus on what his resignation means for the world of artificial intelligence . Le Figaro evokes "an earthquake for the world of AI, and particularly Nvidia's coveted, advanced AI chips". The Financial Times reports that shares plunged as uncertainty over who will succeed Huang grows. Nvidia's CFO Colette Kress will take over for now. As French business daily La Tribune notes, the post-Jensen era of Nvidia has already begun.
In the editorial pages, The Wall Street Journal looks at some of the silver linings that have come out of this crisis. It could harden Congress's resolve to close loopholes in export controls and perhaps "educate Americans about the serious threat of Chinese corporate espionage ." The Chinese government outlet Global Times editors', however, object to the speculation that any ties to China automatically mean a national security threat. They write: "The more accomplished and influential a person is, and the more centrally positioned they are between China and the US, the more vulnerable they may become to being singled out in the name of 'national security.'"
Turning to football news, Zinédine Zidane suffered his first defeat as coach of Les Bleus against Italy on Thursday. Les Bleus played Italy in Milan in the Nations League and amid the rain, they lost 3-1. L'Equipe, the French sports paper, laments Zidane's first defeat as coach. But it's joy and jubilation for Gazzetta dello Sport, the Italian sports daily, which celebrates a "golden Italy."
Finally, there is a bit of good news about last year's viral drunk raccoon. The Independen t reminds us about the raccoon that raided a Virginia liquor store last year, drank 14 bottles of booze and then passed out beside a toilet, its photo swiftly going viral in the process. Now, a local animal shelter has cashed in by merchandising "Trashed Panda" shirts, mugs and hats in honour of the raccoon. It reports that sales have brought in nearly $300,000 for the shelter, far exceeding the shelter's annual $20,000 in donations.

How could the Nvidia CEO’s affair threaten US national security?
Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has been summoned to testify next month before a Senate committee about his alleged affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.
Huang abruptly quit on Thursday as head of one of the world's most valuable companies after revelations of alleged extramarital affairs, in a stunning fall from grace that sent shockwaves through Silicon Valley.
Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who is under scrutiny over exports of sensitive Nvidia AI chips to China, has also been summoned to appear before the Senate Banking Committee in December.
Nvidia has lost $550bn (£415bn) in stock market value in just five days as the scandal dominated headlines.
Senator Tim Scott sent letters on Thursday to Huang and Lutnick requesting their testimony in front of the Senate Banking Committee.
"Recent reports raise serious concerns about our national security and the protection of sensitive US technology," the South Carolina Republican posted on X.
Scott asked Huang to appear voluntarily on 3 December, but also warned the panel could issue a subpoena to compel his testimony.
Three House of Representatives committees - on intelligence and foreign affairs and a panel on China - have also sent a letter to Huang summoning him for a closed-door interview on 1 December.
How a sex scandal at Nvidia is putting pressure on the White House
How AI visionary Jensen Huang was undone by his own bad decisions
Lutnick is under scrutiny because unnamed officials in President Donald Trump's administration have been briefing US media that the commerce secretary stalled efforts to tighten export restrictions on advanced AI chips to China.
A commerce department spokesperson told US media that Lutnick had "proactively" agreed to appear before the Senate Banking Committee.
Huang, who has been Nvidia's public face since 1993, admitted on Sunday to having been "unfaithful" to his wife after reports he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, Alice Huang.
On Wednesday, he was reported to have had a second relationship, this time with an Nvidia executive.
Alice Huang (no relation) worked as an executive at the Singaporean firm Megaspeed. She has been suspected of being an intelligence asset for China, according to the New York Times. China has rejected that allegation as a smear.
Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has also been summoned to appear before the Senate Banking Committee in December
US Attorney General Todd Blanche said on Thursday the Department of Justice had not yet drawn any conclusions about whether Alice Huang was engaged in espionage for Beijing.
Nvidia officials have repeatedly declined to comment since Wednesday. A personal representative of Huang also declined to comment on Thursday.
According to US media, Huang's alleged second affair was with a long-time Nvidia executive, Kimberly Powell, who reported directly to him within the company.
Sources have told the BBC that Nvidia employees had noticed the pair were unusually close.
Who is Nvidia's interim CEO Colette Kress - and who could take over permanently?
The rise and fall of Jensen Huang - how the tech superstar became mired in scandal
Huang had been widely expected to weather the storm after the first affair became public, even as Nvidia announced it had launched an investigation into whether its CEO had been "the target of a foreign intelligence effort".
One current Nvidia staff member told the BBC that the initial reports of his infidelity were more or less brushed off by rank-and-file workers inside the company.
It wasn't until Huang's alleged affair with the Nvidia executive became public that workers started to feel "this is crazy", the person said.
Another Nvidia employee said they had been told not to speak with the press or otherwise comment on the situation in public.
Many staff have earned millions of dollars in compensation through their ability to cash out their Nvidia shares as the stock soared.
Nvidia has said it has "no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised", but pledged that its independent inquiry would look at all available information.
The company's meteoric rise had been led by Jensen Huang, who became a major booster of the AI industry, which relies on Nvidia for the powerful computer chips it manufactures.
But as AI technology evolved in the last four years into chatbots and large language models, companies building AI tools suddenly required huge numbers of the Nvidia computer chips that could process large amounts of data.
Nvidia is now hunting a permanent replacement for Huang. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress was named on Thursday as interim CEO.
Several tech insiders that the BBC spoke with this week noted that Huang's downfall has been a major topic of conversation in San Francisco Bay area circles, an area filled with tech employees, industry executives and billionaires.
Huang has been married to Lori Huang for 40 years. Both of their children are also executives at Nvidia.
Nvidia's stock fall this week is the most significant five-day drop the company has seen since going public 27 years ago.
Its market value rose by more than 470% in the past five years, peaking just a few weeks ago. It is now down by 31% against a backdrop of wider uncertainty in the tech sector.

ChatGPT can now shop for you. On Friday, OpenAI launched a new wallet feature that lets its agents, called dots , help you decide what to buy and then complete the purchase on your behalf. The option will initially be available to a limited number of U.S. ChatGPT Pro subscribers, ages 18 and up, with a U.S.-issued Visa, Mastercard, or American Express.
OpenAI says that users are fully in control of the purchases, as they’re able to review the items, the total, and the payment card that will be used to complete the transaction before the checkout occurs. In addition, users will approve the purchases directly with a security check like Face ID or a fingerprint, which creates a record of their transaction.
The addition comes as consumer-facing AI tools are working to find the right product-market fit, in terms of how they can help people be more efficient as they complete various tasks. While companies like DoorDash and Uber have so far reported low numbers of orders placed by AI agents, Meta’s Muse, which now has over 10 million users, has seen AI-assisted shopping become a top activity on its app.
Other personal AI agents, like Instinct, also support making purchases on users’ behalf.
It’s no surprise, then, that OpenAI would want to enter this space more with an agentic shopping feature of its own.
To get started, ChatGPT subscribers add their eligible payment cards to the new ChatGPT Wallet, then ask their dot to help with a purchase. (This setup is a one-time thing; users don’t have to re-enter their payment information every time they buy.) When it’s time to transact, ChatGPT’s Wallet charges the selected card using a payment token, which is a substitute for the user’s actual card details, so that information isn’t shared with either the dot or the merchant.
The merchant will automatically receive what it needs to fulfill the order from the dot, like the shipping address and contact information, OpenAI says. The company notes that customers who shop via their dots will still be able to earn their credit card rewards and be able to take advantage of protections that typically come with cards, like being able to dispute transactions.
The limited availability at launch will allow OpenAI to test and improve the feature and its capabilities before rolling it out more broadly. In the future, the company plans to offer users more control over the feature by allowing them to set spending limits or configure other parameters around purchase categories or time periods, so they can pre-approve purchases that their agent can then handle more autonomously.
It also aims to make the agentic shopping feature an option at a broader number of supported retailers. This could be a challenge in some areas, where retailers are blocking AI agents from using their site ; on the shopping front, the largest retailer to ban AI agents is Amazon, as it aims to steer users to its own AI agent, Alexa, instead.
To help retailers adapt to agentic commerce, OpenAI also published a Commerce Partner Playbook that offers tools and guidance to sites that want to support customers using agents.

The subscription fee for newly launched Paprika 4 is well worth the price. And the free version is better, too.
Nearly 10 years after the launch of Paprika 3, the recipe-managing, pantry-organizing, grocery list-making app has gotten a big upgrade that adds more functionality to nearly every corner of the experience. I tested Paprika 4 for several weeks while it was in open beta, and the update recently launched across Android (the version I’ve been using), iOS , Windows , and macOS .
Where Paprika 3 was a one-time purchase per platform, accessing most of the new features in Paprika 4 requires an annual subscription fee of $14.99 (it can also be gifted ). With the subscription, you can access the app on any supported platform. New users, as well as those who bought Paprika 3 (or previous versions) but don’t want to pay for the subscription, will be moved to a free version of Paprika 4, which comes with a smaller selection of features that were available to test in beta, plus the ability to save up to 50 recipes.
Together, the new features locked behind the paywall make it possible to import recipes from social media and from physical cookbooks, scan product barcodes to organize your pantry or shopping list, and connect with other cooks via the app to share notes and recipes. They’re good, for the most part, and makes the subscription feel worth it. But the free version is upgraded in ways that make it worth trying if you’re hearing about Paprika for the first time.
My favorite of the new subscription-exclusive features solves a conundrum I often find myself in: My wife sends me a lot of recipe videos on Instagram. I often take screenshots of the text to piece the recipe together. Paprika 4 can pull the pertinent info from those screenshots and build a recipe — that is, if there’s a complete enough recipe in the text to autofill in Paprika’s recipe fields.
As an alternative to feeding the app a screenshot, you can send a social media post from TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, or Facebook to Paprika 4 straight from the share sheet, and it’ll scrape the caption and convert it in a few seconds. It won’t pull info from a video (which would be convenient — and controversial), and it’ll only work if there’s caption text in the photo or video post available to scrape. It sounds limited, but it’s a nice improvement, and it keeps the link to the social media post in the recipe so I can easily go back and view it as needed.
A lot of social media accounts hide their recipes from people scrolling by, requiring an extra step like “comment with TASTYYUMYUM to get my free recipe.” I respect the hustle, even if I hate seeing this as I’m searching for recipes. Paprika unsurprisingly stumbles when recipe posts are too thin on parseable info. But for ones that have enough, it’s really easy to get them into the app.
Paprika 4 also lets you import recipes with your phone camera. I’ve used it to take pictures from cookbooks that we own, and the app converts them accurately. On the free version, you’re limited to copy-pasting website URLs into the app’s browser and having it convert them into recipes that way. It works really well, but feels rudimentary by comparison.
The updated app is stuffed with other new features, several of which are a tad superfluous (and less useful to me) but still seem good to offer when you’re hoping to attract subscribers. For instance, you can compile your recipes into your own digital cookbook to share with other users (this feature is in the free version, too) and set up family sharing — even DMing links within the app to other Paprika users. Family sub-accounts can be added to your account for no extra cost beyond the subscription, so long as they haven’t made a Paprika account with the same email address.
Paprika 4 can guess the nutrition facts of your recipes, which is nice if you have fitness goals or just generally like to know what kind of heat your food is packing, so to speak. I wouldn’t take the results to be totally accurate, but it seems capable enough. This feature is locked behind the subscription paywall.
Another feature I could see myself using more of is the expanded pantry tool. Paprika 3 had a single “pantry,” but the paid and free versions of Paprika 4 let you specify where items are stored, such as in a cupboard, fridge, freezer, and anywhere else. I was also excited about the new barcode scanning feature, a premium feature that can quickly and easily add items to your pantry. While it didn’t work for me in beta, the scanning function works well in the current version. It recognized items that I frequently purchase at Trader Joe’s, Whole Foods, and a bodega. It adds what they are in simple terms (i.e., olive oil spray instead of “Trader Joe’s Organic Extra Virgin Olive Oil Spray”).
The Cook Mode is neat, and is available on both the free and paid versions of Paprika 4. When activated through a drop-down menu, the app reads the first step of the recipe out loud, waiting for you to chime in before continuing. You can ask it to repeat a step, go to the next one, double or halve the recipe, set timers, and strike steps or ingredients as you complete them, among other preset commands and questions . In this mode, the mic stays on by default, though the app won’t respond to unrelated chatter. If asking a prompt doesn’t get it to do anything, you can use the wake word “paprika” to reengage it. This feature has obvious accessibility benefits.
There’s extensive Alexa integration , too, if you pay the subscription fee. It gives Alexa access to your recipes, grocery list, pantry, and meal plan. You can manage grocery lists and pantries by voice with Echo speakers, and screen-equipped Echo devices like the Echo Show can display recipes and support hands-free cooking. The iOS version of Paprika 4 also adds widgets and an array of shortcuts for iOS and macOS, like adding items to a grocery list or pantry, showing scheduled meals in your meal plan, and more . These don’t require a subscription.
For people who are serious about staying organized in the kitchen — both in terms of their pantries and catalog of recipes — these paywalled features will likely get enough use each week to be worth paying for. Though, if you haven’t used Paprika before, the free version is a great place to start.
Even as someone who was content with the features in Paprika 3, I can see the value in paying for the subscription-exclusive features. During the beta, I landed on $2 being a figure I’d be comfortable paying each month for them, and Hindsight Labs settled on just $1.25 per month. It’s going to be getting a lot more money per user than it ever has, but like most Paprika users, I would have purchased the app multiple times over due to how useful it is for me. I guess I get to do that now.

Gone are the days when you could just buy your father a random tie or some leather-clad alcohol vessel or a shaving kit. Dads want — nay, deserve — something memorable. Luckily for you, it’s not that hard to find something special that he’ll approve of, and we’re here to guide you.
We’ve curated this year’s gift list with the modern father in mind, whether he’s a gamer, creator, chef, or simply a gadget lover. There’s a lot in here we think he’ll like, from noise-canceling headphones like the Sonos Ace Ultra and an autonomous drone to a brilliant QD-OLED monitor and a nifty light that’s perfect for illuminating his next campsite. Whatever your dad is into, we’ve got you covered.
Antigravity’s A1 is the ultimate gadget for the dad who dreams of owning the sky. The compact drone comes with specialized goggles that will make him feel like he’s in the cockpit, and it records always-on, 360-degree 8K video. It’s an exhilarating flight experience and an excellent creator’s tool in one slick package.
Cleaning gadgets like Dyson’s PencilVac FluffyCones are never cheap, but they’re often worth the cost and a pleasure to use. The lightweight, broom-replacing stick vacuum doesn’t do carpets, but its rolling bars pack incredible cleaning power for touching up hard floors, including stairs.
For those who love travel but hate the constraints of a hotel TV, Belkin’s ConnectAir is a slick solution. Plug the transmitter into any device with a USB-C video-out port and the receiver into the TV’s HDMI port, and voilà, you’re easily (and wirelessly) connected.
Sonos raised its headphones game on all fronts with the Ace Ultra, which deliver better noise canceling, improved sound, and the feature we’ve all been waiting for: Wi-Fi support. With the ability to bounce audio across your Sonos ecosystem, including from a TV via newer Sonos soundbars, Dad’s sonic sanctuary is finally complete.
Werewolf’s affordable dongle kit provides an almost magical way to power nearly any DC device from a USB-C charger or portable battery. Program it from a mobile app, connect it to your old gear, and everything from a PC monitor to an original Game Boy can accept USB-C charging.

Smart TVs are often pretty dumb. If your dad is always complaining about his TV, or if you want to get ahead of it, grab the latest Apple TV 4K. Although it’s not cheap, it stands out with built-in mics for Siri AI, lots of power, HomePod surround sound support, and a simple, ad-free interface.
The Switch 2 leverages the same ideas as its predecessor, only with a larger, 7.9-inch display, a faster chip, and a bevy of new social features. However, its most important trait is that it’s the newest Nintendo console, which means access to a host of weird, beautiful, family-friendly games that only Nintendo could dream up, now on a better screen.
Oura didn’t reinvent the wheel with the Ring 5, but it did reshape it into a slimmer, thinner, more wearable design that could make all the difference. Inside are the same extensive health and fitness tracking features for charting everything from sleep to heart health, backed by long battery life.
The CS-Pro will make your dad feel like a private eye in the early ’80s. The retro-inspired digital camera serves up 16-megapixel stills and offers four filters accessible from its tactile dial, plus USB-C charging, a high-quality Xenon flash, and a 4GB SD card for plenty of vintage photo fun.
BougeRV’s fancy, compact lamp will spark joy for the glamper in your life, as well as everyone else. Its powerful, foldable spread of LEDs provides a blast of light anywhere plug-ins can’t reach, from the beach to the shed where that scary spider holds court, with up to 60 hours of light on low power.
The Rival Pro offers plenty of thoughtful extras, including swappable batteries and an ultra-wideband base station for a seamless, low-latency connection. The gaming mouse’s lightweight design and 8,000Hz polling rate also deliver both accurate and ergonomic performance for up to 16 hours per charge.
It’s time to help Dad ditch his collection of plastic reusable cups, which have clearly seen better days. NotNeutral’s hand-pressed, timeless tumbler offers ’70s vibes with a modern twist, making it the perfect vessel for whatever Dad twists into his favorite drink.
Give the gift that fixes past home improvement transgressions. These handy Japanese-made pliers from Vampire Tools have one fundamental purpose — to remove stripped screws — and they’re damn good at it. The best part? Watching Dad’s face light up seconds before he sprints to the garage for them.
For the manga or live-action Netflix show lover on your list, this fashionable Pirates jersey, inspired by Monkey D. Luffy from the seminal pirate adventure series One Piece , will be as surprising as it is delightful.
If you’re after a cheap, useful stocking stuffer, Trond’s reliable three-prong extension cord is a practical pick that’s available in leftward or rightward configurations to fit nearly any outlet. Dad will probably say, “Oh, I’ve always wanted one of these,” and this time he’ll mean it.

The new Fitbit Air provides the same great fitness tracking we’ve come to expect in a comfortable design that virtually disappears on your wrist. Uber is notifying thousands of drivers that their personal and driver’s license information was stolen during an October data breach at one of the company’s tech providers.
In notices filed this week with several U.S. attorneys general, including California , the ride-hail giant said it was notified on October 9 by the provider that hackers broke in and stole internal credentials, which were used to access Uber’s data.
The company said it subsequently began notifying affected drivers that their personal information was stored with the provider.
TechCrunch has learned that the provider is Fireworks AI, which lets developers access and use open AI models. Fireworks reported a data breach last month in which hackers stole its customers’ information, including billing data and some private AI datasets.
Online productivity startup Notion confirmed its data was also stolen in the Fireworks hack.
“The notices to drivers are in relation to a security incident impacting one of our third-party vendors, Fireworks.ai, which had access to some Uber data,” an Uber spokesperson told TechCrunch, deferring our questions to Fireworks.
Uber did not say how many customers are affected by the breach, nor how many drivers it was notifying about the incident.
When reached by email, a spokesperson for Fireworks confirmed that the company identified a security issue involving unauthorized access to some of its systems, which affected customer data, but the spokesperson did not address our questions about the incident.
According to data breach notices seen by TechCrunch, the stolen data includes driver’s licenses of 2,567 individuals in Massachusetts, 3,430 people across South Carolina, and 1,873 residents of Rhode Island. A filing with Illinois showed that some state residents had their driver’s license information stolen, but that the number of affected people was pending. Uber also notified drivers who live in California, but did not say how many had their information stolen.
The number is expected to rise as more data breach notifications roll in.
Fireworks attributed its breach to a financially motivated cybercriminal group whose goals are to sell stolen tokens for accessing large language models, or LLMs.
No known cybercriminal group has taken credit for the data theft.
This is Uber’s second known data breach this year. The company reported a security incident at its Uber Freight truck shipping unit, for which an extortion gang took credit for stealing data.

In the last few months, Fireflies , Wispr Flow , and Granola have all released competing capabilities in the dictation and meeting note-taking space. The newest entrant in that category is voice AI giant ElevenLabs , which this week released an experimental app called ElevenAI that combines meeting note-taking, dictation, and agent integration.
Launched during its 11/11 Summit in New York, ElevenAI is still in preview, and you have to sign up for early access instead of just downloading an app. ElevenLabs, valued at $22 billion , is very much positioning this as a product that lives within a team as compared to a productivity tool for an individual.
ElevenAI packs all the features typically found in other apps in the category. It can take meeting notes across your meetings and notify other participants that the conversation is being recorded. Users can query data across meetings and get live assistance during a chat, helping them recall a key detail from older conversations. ElevenLabs also allows companies to integrate ElevenAgent and take follow-up actions such as writing a draft email based on meeting notes.
Plus, there’s a dictation feature, which lets users convert speech to cleaned-up text in any app with support for over 90 languages. The company said that the app is capable of understanding industry-specific terms across dictation and meeting transcription.
ElevenAI allows the company to use its own model as a showcase and also utilize its agent platforms for better context funneling. The startup’s positioning might not be to directly compete in the productivity market, but rather to give enterprise teams an option to not buy licenses to a notetaker and use its solution instead. All meeting-related tools are rushing to become central knowledge hubs for companies while aiming to automate knowledge extraction and follow-up actions
In the last week, the company also launched its v3 series of Scribe speech-to-text models with live transcription capabilities and the ability for companies to fine-tune models using their own data, a tool to pick the right language model based on use case , and a routine creator that automates tasks based on the transcript.

I had agreed to travel to Denver, Colorado, to interview the Nvidia CEO at SIGGRAPH, the annual confab of computer graphics PhDs and practitioners. Early that year I’d conducted a lengthy sit-down interview with Huang for a WIRED magazine feature, which apparently went well enough—both for WIRED and for Nvidia’s executive communications team—that I had been asked to interview Huang again at this conference. Another opportunity to grill the CEO of the modern world’s most consequential company? Yes, of course. I began preparing.
What ensued was, in a word, bizarre. During the first prep call for the conference, the type of call in which PR handlers typically try to coax specific questions out of journalists to prevent an ambush, a youngish, vaguely familiar woman took the lead. This was Madison Huang, Jensen’s daughter. She was clearly intelligent, commanding respect. She told me about the slides Jensen would be presenting on stage at SIGGRAPH and offered suggestions for key moments when I might tee him up to talk about the slides.
I raised my concerns with both my editors and Nvidia. We agreed that I would ask the questions I intended to ask him, which included questions about the environmental impact of data centers, and that Huang would also be referring to slides. Let’s just say the interview didn’t go smoothly. (It’s on YouTube .) To this day, former and current Nvidia workers sometimes tell me that I “handled” the whole thing well. Huang was domineering, evaded some of my questions, and, immediately after our session concluded, did an impromptu Q&A session with a much more adoring crowd than me. Then I was guided offstage, and Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg hopped on, where he and Huang had a lovey-dovey fireside chat.
As a longtime journalist I’m used to occasional adversarial interactions; I really don’t lose sleep over them. This was just a CEO being a CEO. Huang later agreed to meet with me again, in December 2024. But that interview in Denver had underscored for me how much Jensen Huang wanted to control the narrative. Not just wanted to; he assumed he would . And to a large extent he did. Until this week.
Narrative has always been a critical part of Huang’s success. He was not just your average electrical engineering nerd who toiled away on something that would eventually find a product-market fit. By Huang’s own telling, he was an immigrant founder, an underdog, a wife guy who chased (and eventually married) his college sweetheart, a scrappy startup guy who dined at Denny’s in the early days. A visionary who worked Sundays and who didn’t sleep well because he always heard the hoofsteps of competitors. A parent who brought his kids into the corporate fold. A man who loved Nvidia so much he tattooed an abstract version of the company logo on his arm.
Huang built the highest-valued publicly traded company in history. That part’s not just fairy tale. It’s true. Now, it’s starting to read more like a Greek tragedy.
Back in January 2024, when I sat down with him for our first-ever in-person meeting, Huang right off the bat talked about the importance of storytelling. Here’s an excerpt:
Jensen Huang: Somebody who I really admire, as a leader and a person, is Shantanu Narayen, the CEO of Adobe. He said he always wanted to be a journalist because he loved telling stories.
WIRED: It seems like an important part of building a business, being able to tell its story effectively.
Yes. Strategy setting is storytelling. Culture building is storytelling.
You’ve said many times you didn’t sell the idea of Nvidia based on a pitch deck.
Of course, even then, Huang was caught up in the crosshairs of the US–China AI war and at the mercy of regulators, as I wrote at the time. After Donald Trump’s reelection that year, Huang once again deployed his storytelling skills and lobbied the Trump administration to loosen export controls, so he could sell some of his company’s chips to China.
Another crucial part of the Huang lore is that he ran a “flat” organization, with a few dozen top executives reporting to him. (This is sometimes reported as being “60” people; insiders have told me at times it’s closer to 35.) Huang once said the structure allowed Nvidia “to adapt a lot more quickly, which we need because our technology is moving so quickly.” Huang was also known to be controlling of all aspects of the business—participating in every significant meeting, seemingly aware of every moving part, and staying in the loop on sourcing, supply chains, and the company’s allocation of chips.
This is where Huang’s cult of leadership, and his Nvidia storytelling, may have come to a stupidly disappointing final chapter. As one former employee put it, Huang can’t simultaneously have had knowledge of every element of Nvidia’s business and then potentially feign ignorance about where the chips may have fallen, both figuratively and literally. His apparent lapses in judgment have now led him to resign from the very company he coaxed into existence, and have shattered the mythos of its ever-prescient founder.
It’s certainly not the narrative ending Huang would have chosen, were he still in control.

Meta has ticked off academics on all sides of the social media and mental health debate.
Three years ago, Meta apparently considered a plan to turn public opinion against one of its most influential opponents, Jonathan Haidt. But since the proposal was revealed in court filings last month, it’s backfired. In fact, if there’s one thing Anxious Generation author Haidt and his critics can agree on, it’s being mad at Meta.
Recent court filings in California revealed that Meta employees had discussed in 2023 a “ Whisper strategy ” to “turn academics against Haidt,” who would soon publish a bestselling book arguing that platforms like Meta’s were hurting kids. Haidt had spent years popularizing his theory that social media and smartphones are to blame for the decline in teens’ mental health, including in his 2018 book The Coddling of the American Mind and before Congress in 2022 . To counter it, Meta apparently considered a “Below-the-line campaign,” including one idea to “Get Gellman to write a take-down piece” — possibly a reference to Columbia University statistics and political science professor Andrew Gelman, who’d previously publicly critiqued Haidt, though the spelling differs.
Meta employees had discussed in 2023 a “Whisper strategy” to “turn academics against Haidt”
It’s unclear if Meta ever acted on the strategy those employees appeared to consider. But the revelation has stirred up a much louder backlash among both Haidt and his most prominent detractors, most of whom weren’t mentioned by name. Meta declined to comment for this article.
Several academics have come forward to insist Meta had no hand in their opposition to Haidt. “No. I was not paid to critique the Anxious Generation. I came to the conclusion that the science featured in it was flawed all on my own,” reads the title of a Substack post from Candice Odgers, a prominent psychology professor who studies the effects of tech on teens and has frequently critiqued Haidt’s work. “I have never been approached by Meta to shape what I say publicly about the research on adolescents and social media,” Odgers wrote. “My views are my own , and are grounded in the years of research I’ve done on this topic.”
“These days, I have absolutely nothing nice to say about Meta-the-company despite knowing a few amazing people who work there. I think the company is unethical to the core,” wrote danah boyd , a communication professor at Cornell University who has studied how teens use social media . “But I still stand by my research on teens and the research of others who have done rigorous analyses putting teens’ lives into context.”
Haidt is an extremely influential but polarizing figure. Through his bestselling book, The Anxious Generation , and related writing, he has made the case that social media and smartphone access for kids has contributed to a significant decline in mental health. His work has found support among academics including frequent collaborator and San Diego State University psychology professor Jean Twenge, and Haidt has published responses to the debate over his findings. But other longtime researchers in the field say the available evidence does not ultimately support his theory, and social media’s impact on teens at the population level is at most mixed.
Though Gelman has previously critiqued Haidt’s methods, this time he came to his defense, denouncing Meta’s private discussions. “I think it’s horrible for Haidt that this happened to him,” Gelman told The Verge in an interview. He wrote on his blog that he’s “never been contacted by anyone at Facebook or Meta regarding Jonathan Haidt or his work.” While he said he has received money from the company in the past, including a $25,000 “no-strings-attached donation” in 2016 through Columbia for his research, the money has never been related to “social media’s impact on teen health.”
Gelman says that Meta has every right to be in the conversation on the topic — but it should do so openly. “Doing it behind the scenes, it’s creepy. It’s horrible. I have nothing good to say about that,” he said.
“The idea that Meta would create a whisper campaign or whatever against any scholar is gross”
“The idea that Meta would create a whisper campaign or whatever against any scholar is gross,” said Chris Ferguson, a Stetson University psychology professor, in an email to The Verge . Ferguson published a meta-analysis of experimental studies on social media’s impact on mental health that found limited evidence of a causal effect. Ferguson, who said he receives “no funding from Meta or any other tech company,” accused both Haidt and Meta of being “more similar than different.”
“Both have been aggressive, and a pernicious influence on our understanding of youth mental health,” Ferguson wrote, saying that Haidt’s viewpoint is not backed up by science. “It’s possible to view Meta as a big, ugly, cynical, unethical company and, at the same time, view Jonathan Haidt as a pseudoscientist who should know better [than] to peddle nonsense capitalizing on parental fears for profit.”
The Meta meeting notes were disclosed on a court docket for a group of consolidated lawsuits against Meta and other social media companies alleging they misled the public about their services’ safety risks to teens. Meta has recently faced several high-profile legal defeats in similar cases that could cost it billions in penalties , and separately settled claims from state attorneys general for $17.1 billion.
In a statement to The Verge , Haidt said he’s never suggested the researchers named in this article were paid by Meta to critique his work, and hasn’t seen evidence to suggest that. “As a social psychologist who has studied the benefits of viewpoint diversity, I welcome opposing views and civil, rigorous scientific debate. Criticism by these researchers has caused me and my research group to dig deeper and sharpen our arguments,” Haidt says, noting that his research group has published “multiple review papers” laying out evidence that heavy social media use is harmful.
“I am glad to see that so many social scientists are expressing strong criticism of Meta”
“Meta’s own internal studies confirm our finding. Meta’s internal documents also show that the company discussed a plan to distort the academic debate and process, a tactic straight out of the Big Tobacco playbook,” Haidt added. “That should concern anyone who cares about scientific integrity and the well-being of children. I am glad to see that so many social scientists are expressing strong criticism of Meta for doing so.”
Ferguson said it’s not healthy for science to be associated with any one individual, and that Haidt himself could do more to discourage that. “I think people are slowly realizing it’s possible both to believe that Meta is evil and Haidt is full of crap at the same time,” Ferguson said.

First direct attack on US military installations for months was in response to US airstrike on communications tower
Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps says it has targeted and destroyed a US early-warning radar in Bahrain in response to a US airstrike on a communications tower in Sirik overlooking the strait of Hormuz. It is Iran’s first direct attack on US military installations for months.
“This is a serious warning to the aggressor enemy to end its aerial mischief and oil smuggling in the strait of Hormuz,” the IRGC said. “In the event of repeated violations and aggression, the IRGC aerospace force is on full alert to confront the enemy without constraint.”
US Central Command denied that the radar system had been destroyed and said US forces had intercepted two Iranian drones headed for Bahrain .
Donald Trump has said in a series of media interviews over the past 24 hours that he will attack Iran only if necessary, claiming that Gulf countries, such as Saudi Arabia, have urged him to hold back from planned large-scale military strikes.
Trump said he had asked the vice-president, JD Vance, to end his interest in negotiating a new deal with Iran and instead focus on corruption and fraud in Democrat-run cities and states.
Vance had been seen by the Iranians as the most trustworthy figure close to Trump, but they had rejected his request for a personal meeting with their negotiators to discuss the terms of a peace deal.
Vance has been at the forefront of Republicans saying the war was the cause of the widespread Republican losses in the midterms. Trump said he had been disappointed in the American public because higher diesel prices were a small price to pay for preventing Iran from acquiring a nuclear weapon.
An opinion poll in the UK showed 65% of the British public would oppose the US resuming the war in Iran, and only 14% would back it. The poll was conducted by YouGov for the Council for Arab-British Understanding (Caabu).
It also found 54% oppose UK bases being used by the US to mount attacks on Iran, with 29% in favour. Support for additional UK sanctions against Iran was 45%, with 22% opposed.
The poll was conducted on Tuesday and Wednesday this week, before two Iranians were found guilty on Thursday of spying and planning attacks on journalists in the UK. The Iranian embassy has rejected the court judgment as an attempt to advance a political agenda.
Chris Doyle, the director of Caabu, said: “The British public are sceptical about any war on Iran and what it might achieve. What might make the Burnham government take note is the very high level of opposition to any further war amongst 2024 Labour voters, at 79%.”
Iran’s Assembly of Experts, a body of elected Islamic jurists responsible for choosing the supreme leader, has become the first governing institution in Iran to call for a review of the country’s defence doctrine, potentially leading to religious permission for Iran to try to acquire a nuclear weapon.
In a statement released on Thursday, the assembly called for a review of Iran’s membership of the nuclear non-proliferation treaty, describing the move as an “unavoidable necessity” and a “public and national demand”.
The intervention carries a religious as much as political significance because the 88-strong assembly comprises senior clerics, most of whom are supposed to be qualified to exercise independent Islamic legal reasoning.
Iran has had a longstanding prohibition on nuclear weapons, based on a fatwa issued by the late supreme leader Ali Khamenei, but the relevance of the fatwa in the wake of the US attacks on Iran has been questioned widely in political and security circles.
Whether Iran has the stockpiles of uranium or technology to build a nuclear weapon is contested.
The UN nuclear inspectorate has expressed alarm about a continued lack of information from Iran about its nuclear sites. It said: “Our concerns are growing over Iran’s refusal to allow access to design information or inspections of the Isfahan facility. We do not know the exact location of the Isfahan uranium enrichment facility or whether it contains nuclear materials. It is imperative that we carry out our verification activities in Iran without further delay.”

Senator Chris Van Hollen’s policy credentials allowed his quick rise to roles usually reserved for the more tenured
US senator Chris Van Hollen’s challenge to Chuck Schumer ’s leadership of Senate Democrats presents an ideological and biographical contrast to the party as it takes control of Congress in two months.
Though only about eight years younger than Schumer, Van Hollen is seen as a more progressive senator who has drawn attention for his opposition to the Trump administration ’s abusive immigration practices – visiting his constituent Kilmar Ábrego García after an unlawful deportation to El Salvador – as well as opposition to federal corruption and US support for the Israeli government’s war in Gaza.
Van Hollen’s father was a diplomat and his mother was a spy. Born in Karachi and raised abroad before returning to the US for high school in Massachusetts, Van Hollen, 67, earned a philosophy degree from Swarthmore College, then a masters of public policy concentrating in national security studies from Harvard’s John F Kennedy school of government. He worked as a US Senate staffer while studying for a law degree from Georgetown University, which he earned in 1990.
He won a seat in the Maryland house of delegates in the same year, representing Montgomery county, and developed a reputation for fierce advocacy for environmental causes, gun control and public education. Four years later, he won a state senate seat, which he held until challenging a popular moderate Republican congresswoman, Constance A Morella, in 2002. Democrats nationally took a beating that year; Van Hollen’s success was an outlier.
Van Hollen’s policy credentials and longstanding political relationships allowed him to rise quickly into congressional leadership roles usually reserved for more tenured congresspeople. He chaired the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee, the House fundraising arm for electing Democrats, taking over for Rahm Emanuel in 2008. Van Hollen was a key congressional negotiator during the Great Financial Crisis.
When US senator Barbara Mikulski retired after 30 years in office in 2016, Van Hollen emerged as the favored successor by Maryland’s political establishment and had the support of Senate Democratic leader Harry Reid. Van Hollen became the Senate’s chief fundraiser.
Despite this role, Van Hollen has long opposed the Citizens United ruling that opened the floodgates for corporate spending on political campaigns. Van Hollen was one of dozens of lawmakers who filed an amicus brief in the case to defend federal spending limits and has repeatedly called for a constitutional amendment to overturn the decision.
Van Hollen has also been one of senate Democrats’ sharpest critics of the Israeli government and its actions in Gaza. Long a supporter of a two-state solution, Van Hollen visited the Rafah crossing between Egypt and Gaza in January 2024 to observe aid shipments, declaring the assistance process “broken”. Van Hollen subsequently voted for a resolution proposed by US senator Bernie Sanders to apply the human rights provisions of the Foreign Assistance Act to US military aid to Israel. The resolution failed 72-11, with most Democrats also opposing the measure.
Van Hollen authored a report in November 2025 which described the war as a “plan to ethnically cleanse Gaza of Palestinians”, and that “America is complicit.” Van Hollen has worked to end arms shipments to Israel and opposes American security agreements with Israel in the National Defense Authorization Act.
Van Hollen is also a critic of cryptocurrency and decentralized finance in ways that distinguish him from Schumer and Democratic political ties to the New York financial markets.
“As we’ve seen time and again, cryptocurrency and digital assets are rife with opportunity for abuse if left unchecked,” Van Hollen said in a statement opposing the Clarity Act, a financial regulatory package offered by Republicans. Van Hollen has pursued legislation to ban federal officials from owning or promoting cryptocurrency, pointedly highlighting the president’s billion-dollar gains.
Speaking in post-election interviews last week, Van Hollen argued that Democrats “should not be overly cautious in going after corporations, billionaires and special interests that voters blame for making their lives harder”.

Police confirm sixth victim in DC condo shooting; suspect dead after barricading himself and starting a fire.
Police have said a sixth person was shot on Thursday morning in Washington, DC , bringing the toll to one person killed and five wounded in an attack they believe was linked to a dispute over maintenance issues in a condo building.
In an updated statement, the Metropolitan Police Department said investigators had found a sixth victim, a woman, after officers initially located five other victims.
She was conscious and breathing with a “non-life-threatening gunshot graze wound”.
Two women and two men were taken to hospital, all conscious and breathing.
James Stuart, the 46-year-old manager of the building in which the suspect lived, died at the scene.
Police believe the suspect, a 55-year-old doctor named Matt Wade Lambert, targeted Stuart while Stuart was doing his morning workout at the gym.
The shooting started just before 8am local time (13:00 GMT) at a VIDA Fitness gym in the city’s Logan Circle neighbourhood, about a mile north of the White House.
Police said Lambert shot Stuart inside the gym on the ground floor of the building before going back to his apartment on the seventh floor and firing on people below from his patio.
Five others, some of whom had been working at a construction site across the street. Police have not detailed the circumstances in which the sixth victim was shot.
The shootings unfolded in less than five minutes, according to interim police chief Jeffery Carroll.
Lambert then barricaded himself inside his apartment, where he talked to police negotiators over the phone. Police say he fired at least twice through the door while officers were outside, but no officers were injured.
He also broke the gas line connected to his fireplace and started a fire, which the building’s sprinkler system contained.
Police said Lambert spent most of the conversation with negotiators talking about the dispute with building management.
“Most of the conversation was about the homeowners associations and challenges with that,” said Carroll.
“While our negotiators were communicating with the suspect, they did hear a single gunshot,” he said, adding that Lambert then stopped talking.
When tactical officers forced their way into the apartment, they found him dead from an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound.
Police said inside the apartment, they found a shotgun, a rifle, and a handgun, all of which had been used in the shooting.
According to court records cited by The Associated Press, Lambert had filed a lawsuit alleging that he had not been able to enjoy his penthouse since 2024 because of mould, moisture and water problems that began after work had been done on the building’s exterior.
The lawsuit was ongoing, and Lambert appeared to have shared details of the dispute, including photos and an engineering report on an X account called ofMiceandMold.
His lawyer, Joel Braithwaite, told reporters on Thursday that the condo where Lambert had lived since 2017 looked like “a warzone” and that Lambert had spent more than $300,000 on the lawsuit.

Gunman killed one person and injured at least five others in and around condo building not far from the White House
More details were emerging on Friday about the previous morning’s shooting in north-west Washington DC, as a manager at the shooter’s residential building shared how he was angry over living conditions there and confessed to the killings.
The gunman killed one person and injured at least five others on Thursday in and around the condominium building in the Logan Circle neighborhood of the capital, not far from the White House, where he lived.
Police identified the gunman as 55-year-old Matt Lambert, a doctor who had been involved in an ongoing legal dispute with his building’s management. The person killed was identified as James Stuart, 46, a manager at the condominium complex.
According to police, Lambert fatally shot Stuart inside a gym in his building just before 8am ET, before returning to his apartment, where he fired at four people from his balcony. Those victims were taken to hospital, and as of Thursday, one was in critical condition. Lambert then barricaded himself inside his unit, and was found dead with a self-inflicted gunshot wound.
On Friday morning, DC authorities said that there was an additional victim, whom they described as a woman with a “non-life-threatening gunshot graze wound”.
Charelle Ferguson, another building manager, recalled speaking with Lambert by phone at around 9am that morning, about an hour after the shooting began, she said in an interview with the Washington Post .
Ferguson told the newspaper that she had been calling residents to check on their safety after shots were fired, when Lambert answered. During the conversation, she said that he told her that he was tired of mold and water damage in his apartment.
“The only way people will pay attention, you have to do something,” Ferguson said he told her. She said that he then confessed over the phone to her to shooting the five people.
“I never thought he’d do something like this,” Ferguson told the Post. She also said that he had previously told her about the issues in his unit, and she said she had been sympathetic to his concerns.
Court records seen by the Guardian show that Lambert sued his condo association in 2025, alleging it had failed to address water damage, mold and moisture issues in his apartment, which he alleged began after exterior work was carried out on the building. The association denied allegations of negligence and denied responsibility for the damage in court filings, and the litigation remained ongoing.
Lambert’s attorney in the civil matter, Joel Braithwaite, said at a news conference on Thursday that he was “deeply shocked” by what happened and that he had last spoken with his client on Tuesday and said that he had sounded fine.
“I can’t tell you how surprised I am because the person I knew as a client is someone who is in the business of healing people,” Braithwaite said.
On Thursday evening, residents gathered at a vigil in the neighborhood, lighting candles and showing support for those affected by the shooting.

At least 24 people have been ⁠⁠killed and 11 others injured, after a container truck collided with a bus in ⁠⁠India’s northeastern state of Assam, police said.
The crash happened on Friday on a highway in Golaghat district, near Kaziranga National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site famous for its one-horned rhinos, about 225km (140 miles) east of the state capital, Dispur.
Several children and the bus driver were among the dead, officials said, as Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said on X he was “deeply distressed by the tragic accident”.
“The scale of this loss has shaken all of us, and my heart goes out to every family that has lost a loved one. No words can ease their pain, but I want them to know that they are not alone. All of Assam stands with them in this hour of grief,” Sarma said.
He added that local authorities were at the site and “personally overseeing the relief arrangements … to make sure the injured receive the best possible medical care without delay”.
Swapnaneel Deka, superintendent of police of Golaghat district, told the Reuters news agency that “it is likely the death toll will increase”. He said the bus ⁠⁠was travelling to a neighbouring district, with about 30 people on board.

Finland says Ukraine struck a Russian warship near its coast as Kyiv and Moscow held US-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi.
Finland’s military says it detected “a strike” on a Russian warship in the Gulf of Finland on Wednesday, as Ukraine sent waves of drones towards Russia’s northwestern Leningrad region.
The strike came as Russian and Ukrainian delegations met in Abu Dhabi for their first United States-brokered talks since February.
It was a rare strike on a Russian navy vessel in the Baltic Sea .
So why is Ukraine taking the war to the Baltic, and why now? Here’s what we know:
“The Finnish Defence Forces detected… a strike on a Russian warship in the Gulf of Finland area and has monitored the development of the situation,” a military spokesperson told the Reuters news agency in an emailed statement.
The spokesperson said Finland was not under any immediate military threat, but declined to say where or when the incident happened, or how it had been detected.
It was not immediately clear whether there were any casualties. Estonian media reported that the vessel was a small Russian navy ship that later returned to St Petersburg.
On Wednesday, drones also caused a fire in the Russian port area of Ust-Luga, injuring three workers, regional Governor Aleksandr Drozdenko said.
Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania told citizens to take shelter as drones strayed into their airspace, and NATO scrambled warplanes in response.
The Gulf of Finland is a narrow arm of the Baltic Sea between Finland and Estonia, both NATO members, that extends east to St Petersburg. Ust-Luga, on its southern shore, is a key export outlet for Russian oil and grain.
Several Ukrainian drones deployed towards the Leningrad region have strayed into the airspace of Finland and the Baltic states, raising fears that the war is spilling over into NATO countries that border Russia.
Finland’s Defence Minister Antti Hakkanen said Helsinki had raised the strike with Kyiv.
“We have told the Ukrainians this time, and a little earlier too, how sensitive this narrow stretch of the Gulf of Finland, right between us and Estonia, is in terms of environmental safety and the safety of civilian shipping,” he said, according to Finnish broadcaster Yle.
But he said the spillover effects in the surrounding region stem from Ukraine’s defensive fight and assured the public the Baltic Sea around Finland was still safe.
Ilya Timtchenko, a fellow with the Transatlantic Defense and Security Program at the Center for European Policy Analysis, told Al Jazeera the strike was thought to be the first by Ukrainian forces on a Russian ship in an area of the Baltic used by civilian traffic.
“Ukraine and its European allies are showing that they are unified in their approach to fighting off the Russian threat,” he told Al Jazeera.
Ukraine’s Security Service said it attacked the Buyan-M-class small missile ship, Naro-Fominsk, as part of a special operation, according to Yle.
Meanwhile, Ukraine’s General Staff said the strike on Ust-Luga had damaged five fuel tanks.
“According to preliminary information, as a result of drone strikes on the port’s oil infrastructure, the tank network suffered the most damage,” it reported on Telegram.
On Thursday, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy met US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner in Ireland and praised their mediation efforts.
Russia, Ukraine and the US held two days of talks in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday and Wednesday. The last such talks took place in February this year.
The talks produced no breakthrough, apart from an agreement to swap a large number of prisoners. Russia’s state-run TASS news agency said the exchange should happen in two to three weeks.
Ukraine wants Russia pushed back to the original border between the two countries, while Russian President Vladimir Putin wants to control all of Ukraine’s Donbas region.
Moscow’s demands reach beyond Ukraine as well, focusing also on the expansion of NATO.
Russian negotiators proposed in Abu Dhabi that Finland, which joined the alliance in 2023, leave NATO and that the alliance be barred from having military bases in Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania, the German newspaper Bild reported on Friday.
The informal proposals, shared with European representatives, also called for arrangements to guarantee freedom of navigation in the Black Sea and the Baltic Sea, Bild reported.
On Thursday, Witkoff and Kushner met Putin in Moscow, where the two sides agreed to continue the talks, before the envoys met Zelenskyy in Ireland.
“Kyiv continues to demonstrate two points simultaneously: That it is willing to negotiate and that it has a position of strength,” Timtchenko said. “In parallel with any peace talks, Ukraine will likely continue to strike Russia’s military and the sources of funding for Russia’s war machine.”
Ukraine has repeatedly targeted Russian refineries, ports, and energy infrastructure to raise the economic cost of Moscow’s war effort.
But the strikes have drawn criticism from Washington. Trump has blamed Ukraine’s attacks on Russian energy infrastructure for rising diesel prices, and last month he waived sanctions on Russia that Congress had overwhelmingly approved.
Timtchenko said the strikes still gave Kyiv leverage. “Long-range strikes considerably strengthen Ukraine’s hand at the negotiating table, which is why Russian officials keep bringing them up,” he said.
Russia has not commented publicly on the reported strike on its warship.
Governor Drozdenko said 150 drones were shot down over the Leningrad region during Wednesday’s attack, which also cut off a power station.
“Moscow might voice harsh rhetoric and try to blame the Ukrainians for undermining the peace talks,” Timtchenko said. “However, this is nothing new, since Russia has done this numerous times before.
“Despite Moscow’s pretence of seeking an end to the war, Russia continues to strike Ukraine’s military, critical infrastructure, and civilians,” he added.
